cases.name: two equal paths overlap
cases.why: Two paths overlap only if they are equal after normalization.

cases.name: two different paths do not overlap
cases.why: Two paths overlap only if they are equal after normalization.

cases.name: a leading ./ is ignored
cases.why: A leading `./` is removed before the comparison.

cases.name: a repeated slash is ignored
cases.why: `//` is the same as `/`.

cases.name: a backslash is a separator
cases.why: `\` is replaced by `/`.

cases.name: a .. segment is not resolved
cases.why: The claims dialect does not resolve `..`. The policy dialect does.

cases.name: paths that differ in case do not overlap
cases.why: The claims dialect is case-sensitive. The policy dialect is not: see `the path is compared without case` in the policy fixture `evaluate-paths`.

cases.name: a glob that differs in case from a path does not overlap
cases.why: The claims dialect is case-sensitive for globs too.

cases.name: a glob overlaps a path that it matches
cases.why: A glob and a path overlap if the glob matches the path.

cases.name: a path overlaps a glob that matches it
cases.why: The order of the two arguments does not matter.

cases.name: a * glob does not overlap a deeper path
cases.why: `*` does not cross `/`.

cases.name: dir/** does not overlap the directory itself
cases.why: The claims dialect has no rule that makes `dir/**` match `dir`. The policy dialect has that rule.

cases.name: **/ in the middle matches zero directories
cases.why: `a/**/b` matches `a/b`.

cases.name: a class matches a listed character
cases.why: `[ab]` matches one of the listed characters.

cases.name: [!] matches a slash
cases.why: `[!]` is a negated class with no members, which matches any one character, as in the policy dialect.

cases.name: a negated class with members matches a slash
cases.why: `[!a]` matches every character that is not `a`, `/` included, as in the policy dialect.

cases.name: a negated class does not match one character outside the Basic Multilingual Plane
cases.why: A class matches one UTF-16 code unit, and U+1F600 is two, as in the policy dialect.

cases.name: a class whose range holds the slash matches a slash
cases.why: `[.-0]` is the range from `.` to `0`, which holds `/`.

cases.name: [^] matches a line feed
cases.why: `[^]` is the same as `[!]`, and it matches a line terminator.

cases.name: [!]x] is [!] followed by x and ]
cases.why: The class ends at the first `]` after its first character.

cases.name: a class whose first character is ] does not match its other member
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The seventh open question of the README records the behavior.

cases.name: a class whose first character is ] does not match that character
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The seventh open question of the README records the behavior.

cases.name: []] does not match ]
cases.why: The reference reads `[]` as a class that matches nothing, so the glob matches no path. The seventh open question of the README records the behavior.

cases.name: a ? does not match two characters
cases.why: `?` matches exactly one character.

cases.name: ** does not match a line feed
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators, as in the policy dialect.

cases.name: ** does not match a carriage return
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

cases.name: ** does not match U+2028
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

cases.name: ** does not match U+2029
cases.why: `**` matches any run of characters except the four line terminators.

cases.name: * matches a line feed
cases.why: Only `**` excludes the line terminators. `*` excludes only `/`.

cases.name: two equal paths with a line feed overlap
cases.why: A path is compared as text, so a line terminator in it changes nothing.

cases.name: two globs overlap when one literal prefix starts the other
cases.why: Two globs overlap if the literal prefix of one is a prefix of the other.

cases.name: two globs under different directories do not overlap
cases.why: Neither literal prefix starts the other, and neither glob matches the other prefix.

cases.name: a glob with an empty literal prefix overlaps every glob
cases.why: An empty prefix is a prefix of everything. The comparison reports more overlaps than exist, on purpose.

cases.name: two globs with the same prefix overlap even if no path matches both
cases.why: `a/*.ts` and `a/*.js` share the prefix `a/`. The comparison reports more overlaps than exist, on purpose.

cases.name: the literal prefix ends at a [ that starts no class
cases.why: The literal prefix of `src/a[b` is `src/a`, although its `[` starts no class and matches itself. The two prefixes are equal, so the globs overlap.

description: Whether two patterns of the claims dialect overlap.
